executiveSummary: GM0547's identity, Zuid-Holland province and Hollands-Midden safety-region assignment are coherent. The fresh 2025 boundary contains the generated centre and CBS reports 27,751 residents; twenty neighbourhood rows sum to 27,730 (-21, -0.076%), a negligible annual rounding/suppression difference. The bundle contains three districts, twenty neighbourhoods, one BAG place and one BRT woonkern. Four logical boundary links represent A4 and two short N-road connections; the two A4 links are portions of one physical corridor and are not independent redundancy. No ProRail station lies inside the municipality and 44 scheduled-transit stops are present. All ten presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services and pass structural/numerical contracts. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Official local evidence distinguishes primary-defence breach exposure in the north/northeast, regional-defence breach exposure in central neighbourhoods, Rijnland boezem/polder drainage and street/tunnel water nuisance including Oude Spoorbaan. The generic river and coastal presets select none of these cases, while eight unrelated single-hazard presets reuse exactly the same complete neighbourhood rank: 350-resident Elisabethhof leads and 3,505-resident Ouderzorg is last. A current official 17 August–11 September 2026 Spanjaardsbrug/Lage Rijndijk restriction affecting cars and buses is absent from the context, although emergency, cycle and moped passage remains possible. Alrijne Leiderdorp is a regional 24/7 acute-care destination, but annual facility facts are not live acceptance or capacity. Exact utilities, mobility, supply and first-72-hour recovery remain unsupported by live topology, state, resources and actions. Missing observations, forecasts and registry matches are Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.title: E01 — Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025, table 86165NED, OData API
supports: The official municipality row identifies GM0547 Leiderdorp and reports 27,751 residents, density 2,414 per square kilometre, 23.9% age 65 or older and 4,679 one-person households.

The twenty published neighbourhood rows sum to 27,730 residents (-21, -0.076%), 12,695 households and 6,645 residents aged 65 or older; the negligible difference retains annual rounding and suppression semantics.

Most fields cover all twenty neighbourhoods. Home value, tenure, cars per household and benefit/pension fields cover eighteen; doctor and supermarket distance cover twenty; district-heating share and public-charging counts cover zero and must remain Unknown/NoData rather than zero.

CBS OData is machine-readable under CC BY 4.0, with quarterly additions described for this annual table. It controls residents, not incident-time patients, pupils, visitors, commuters, responders, individual vulnerability or preparedness.

evidenceSources.publisher: PDOK / CBS / Kadaster / Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi
evidenceSources.title: E02 — Full municipal geometry, settlement and road, rail and scheduled-transit reference inputs
evidenceSources.edition: 2025 boundary/statistics and current generated BAG, BRT, NWB, ProRail and GTFS snapshots
supports: The generated centre [4.543414782207039, 52.156011459204294] lies inside the fresh full-resolution 2025 municipal boundary.
The bundle retains three districts, twenty neighbourhoods, one BAG place named Leiderdorp and one BRT woonkern; no BAG place centre falls outside the generalized boundary.

The graph has four logical boundary records: two A4 sections to Leiden and Kaag en Braassem share physical corridor NWB-road-4, plus very short N446 and N445 links to Kaag en Braassem. A4 sections are series, not independent evacuation/supply capacity.

No ProRail station lies inside GM0547 and 44 GTFS stop areas are assigned. Static geometry/timetables do not prove incident-time road, bridge or bus operation, accessibility, destination or throughput.

CBS boundary OGC is half-yearly/CC BY 4.0; BAG is daily/Public Domain Mark 1.0; BRT is CC BY 4.0; NWB is monthly/CC0 1.0; ProRail is manually refreshed/CC0 1.0. OVapi GTFS is free-use best-effort context without an operational SLA.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Adaptatiestrategie Klimaatbestendig Leiderdorp and Integraal Waterketenprogramma 2024–2028
evidenceSources.edition: Strategy dated 24 October 2023 and adopted 18 December 2023; IWKp 2024–2028 current
supports: The municipal strategy says Leiderdorp's relatively low position can yield 0.5–0.8 metre water depths in the north/northeast after a primary-defence breach, while a regional-defence breach can yield depths up to 0.5 metre in central neighbourhoods. These are planning/stress-test scenarios, not a selected live breach.

It identifies observed foundation damage from drought, degraded surface-water quality, urban-green drought stress, street and tunnel water nuisance including Oude Spoorbaan, and insufficient cooling on functional squares.

The IWKp says extreme showers can exceed sewer capacity and temporary water on streets cannot always be prevented. Programme standards and intended measures do not prove incident-time inlet, sewer, storage, pump or receiving-water capacity/state.

The source establishes materially different primary, regional, pluvial, drought and heat pathways at neighbourhood scale. Its public PDF does not itself provide a stable machine incident feed, blanket operational SLA, live state or explicit native-raster NoData contract.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Rijnland polder/boezem management and public GM0547 water-asset snapshot
evidenceSources.edition: Current water-area planning context; HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: Rijnland manages water levels by polder and assesses water nuisance, drought, target levels and measures through water-area plans; this establishes managed boezem/polder pathways rather than an undifferentiated major-river scalar.

The partial HWH snapshot assigns twelve objects to GM0547: one sewer pump, nine surface-water pumps and two sluices/weirs. Named objects include polder Achthoven, Bospolder, Kalkpolder, Munniken/Zijllaan/Meijepolder, Hoogmadeseweg, De Bloemerd, Keersluis Achthovenerweg and Klepstuw de Zijl.

Published capacity values are incomplete/null for several assets and are not safely comparable without native units and function. The contributor-dependent national aggregation is CC BY-SA 4.0 and not proof of complete topology or current operation.
No public record establishes catchment and defence connectivity, boezem/polder levels, comparable capacity, command/settings, blockage, maintenance, power/backup, current state or T+72 restoration.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel Hollands Midden and first-72-hour preparedness
evidenceSources.edition: Current published regional risk profile and municipality risk page; national preparedness guidance current at access
supports: The profile distinguishes primary-defence failure, which is extremely unlikely and associated with severe northwesterly storm plus extreme sea levels, from regional-defence failure caused for example by high boezem levels or instability, with smaller but still serious footprint.

Its regional-defence appendix says outcomes depend on breach location/size, velocity and terrain and can affect power, water/drainage, gas, telecom and transport. Expert breach cases exist, but uncertainty remains and a generic scalar is not a selected case.

The Leiderdorp municipality page lists flooding, nature fire, extreme weather, earthquakes and disruption of gas, electricity, drinking water, wastewater, telecom and food among preparedness-relevant risks. Listing is not event probability, footprint, magnitude or live service state.

National guidance advises a 72-hour kit including three litres of water per person per day, food, medicine, radio/power and a personal plan. Guidance does not prove household readiness, municipal stock or distribution capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: IPLO / Watermanagementcentrum Nederland / KNMI / Rijkswaterstaat / NDW
evidenceSources.title: E06 — LIWO scenario semantics and public observation, forecast, warning and road screens
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO release 2025.1.6; deployment public-context snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: LIWO is a professional scenario system requiring specialist interpretation. A usable flood case must retain source, breach/defence scenario, footprint, units/datum, arrival/duration/recession, probability, CRS, resolution, edition, licence and NoData; it is not a live observation by default.

No GM0547 Waterinfo observation, Waterinfo forecast, KNMI weather-station observation, seismic, RIVM PM2.5 or NDW road-situation record is assigned in the public context. Absence is a coverage/time result, not dry, calm, clean, open or safe.
One province-warning record explicitly reports no warning at its issue time. It is not gridded local forcing and cannot validate an arbitrary exercise horizon.
All these context records remain affectsSimulation=false; observations, forecasts, official scenarios and synthetic model values retain distinct evidence classes and valid times.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Dated Spanjaardsbrug restriction, bridge operation and Zuid-Holland Noord bus context
evidenceSources.edition: Restriction valid 17 August–11 September 2026; Doesbrug 2026 summer schedule; Qbuzz concession current
supports: From 17 August through 11 September 2026, Lage Rijndijk between Sumatrastraat and Spanjaardsbrug is officially closed to cars and buses for Liander gas-main work. Traffic is detoured via Sumatrastraat, Willem de Zwijgerlaan, Engelendaal and Zijldijk; emergency services, cycles and mopeds can pass.

The notice includes direction-specific Baanderij access. It overlaps the audit reference time and full T+72 horizon, but the deployment contains no matching transport restriction. A calendar-unbound preset must not silently activate it; a 3 September 2026 reference run should surface/apply it by mode, direction and valid time.
Doesbrug has a published 2026 summer operating schedule through 26 October. Movable-bridge schedule is contextual availability, not proof of incident-time opening, passability or emergency priority.

Province Zuid-Holland identifies Qbuzz as the Zuid-Holland Noord concession operator from December 2024 through 2037. A concession and 44 GTFS stops do not prove trips operate, detours are encoded or emergency demand can be carried.

evidenceSources.publisher: RIVM / Alrijne Ziekenhuis / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Leiderdorp acute care and public utility, antenna and education context
evidenceSources.edition: RIVM questionnaire 2026 v1.1 published 3 July 2026; deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026
supports: RIVM assigns Alrijne Ziekenhuis, Simon Smitweg 1, inside GM0547 with 24/7 emergency and acute-obstetric provision, twenty treatment rooms and 33,265 visits in 2025. Alrijne confirms that Leiderdorp is its only emergency-department location and access uses A4/N11/Persant Snoepweg corridors.

Annual offer and visits are not incident-time acceptance, staffing, occupancy, triage, ambulance availability, generator/fuel, supplies or throughput. Its regional role creates inbound patient, staff and supply demand beyond CBS residents.

One postcode sample, 2353GA, maps to Liander area OS LEIDERDORP 10-1i: withdrawal existing/required/queue 22/23/2.2 MW with eleven requests, injection 28/10/11 MW with request count null, and twelve projects from 2026. Null remains Unknown, never zero; planning is not feeder topology or live outage.

The screens contain 42 RDI antenna sites—22 mobile, seven fixed-link, eleven amateur and two broadcast—and seventeen DUO education records—eleven primary, one secondary, two special and three other. Registers do not establish coverage/backhaul/power, occupants, shelter role, supplies or operation.

RIVM data are CC0 1.0. DUO's 31 August snapshot is daily under CC Attribution version unspecified. RDI cadence and reuse licence are unstated; the capacity map is planning context without a stable public operational contract. All remain affectsSimulation=false.

The representative centre lies inside the fresh full-resolution 2025 boundary.
Annual registers, static assets/plans, timestamped observations, forecasts, official scenarios and synthetic outputs remain distinct evidence classes.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent river/compound disruption and exact recovery lack incident, action, constraint and resource evidence through T+72.
notes: River severity/stress and seven services remain fixed T+24–72, affected grows 5,794 to 6,480 and Facilities falls 0.736255 to 0.610898, accumulating 523,982.971 person-hours without a selected breach, water balance, access or action.

Storm/pluvial/winter/wildfire direct effects return to zero by T+72 with exact residual service curves; coastal direct water returns to zero but 4,021 remain affected. No pumping, drainage, road clearance, welfare, hospital, utility crew or restocking state explains these values.
Sustained disruption can be plausible, but exact first-72-hour deterioration, plateaus and recovery require selected incidents, measured/modelled state, constraints, resources and actions.

findings.summary: Generic river/coastal outputs conflate distinct primary, regional and polder/boezem pathways without selecting a defensible case.
findings.evidence: Official strategy differentiates 0.5–0.8 m planning depths in northern/northeastern Leiderdorp after primary-defence breach from up-to-0.5 m central exposure after regional-defence breach. VRHM ties these to different triggers/probabilities and says breach geometry, velocity and terrain matter. Yet river holds severity 0.229952/stress 0.739045 through T+72 with affected rising 5,794 to 6,480; coastal reaches normalized stress 1.745917 and 15,272 affected without a named defence, breach, source, footprint, units, arrival or recession.
findings.action: Suppress decision-grade direct flood values until an expert selects a versioned Rijnland/WMCN/LIWO case. Retain primary versus regional defence, breach/source, boezem/polder/control state, terrain-connected footprint, depth/velocity units/datum, arrival, duration/recession, probability, CRS/resolution, licence and NoData. Keep indirect national-network effects separately typed.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated single hazards reuse one complete Leiderdorp neighbourhood order.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank Elisabethhof first, then Kerkwijk, Buitenhof-Oost-Zuid, Schansen en Dreven and Winkelhof, with De Baanderij, Boterhuispolder and Ouderzorg at the bottom. Elisabethhof has about 350 residents while Ouderzorg has 3,505 and is the largest neighbourhood. The same ordering cannot represent defence breach, pluvial drainage, heat, cyber targets, fire/smoke and infrastructure failure.
findings.action: Replace the common municipality seed with hazard-specific source, eligible-domain, forcing, exposed-object and support adapters over full polygons. Add cross-preset tests that unrelated hazards cannot silently share all ranks; missing compatible spatial evidence renders Unknown rather than precise ordering.

findings.summary: Pluvial and Drainage precision ignores known street/tunnel nuisance and Rijnland polder/boezem operating state.
findings.evidence: At T+24 pluvial reports severity 0.603914, normalized stress 0.836188, 9,068 affected and Drainage 0.295928 although rain is zero at that checkpoint. Official sources identify sewer exceedance and Oude Spoorbaan street/tunnel nuisance; twelve public water objects identify Achthoven, Bospolder, Kalkpolder, De Bloemerd, De Zijl and Munniken/Zijllaan/Meijepolder pathways. No rain hyetograph/surface, AHN/street flow, antecedent soil/groundwater, sewer/inlet/storage, receiving levels, pump/sluice topology, power or command drives the value.
findings.action: Integrate a versioned municipal/Rijnland stress case with hyetograph, AHN/BGT, sewer-included flag, street/tunnel flow, groundwater, boezem/polder receiving state, resolution, units, licence and NoData. Join assets only after authority review of catchment/connectivity, native capacity unit, settings, condition, control, power/backup and valid time.

findings.summary: A current mode- and direction-specific Spanjaardsbrug restriction is absent while exact Mobility assumes an incomplete graph.
findings.evidence: The official notice closes Lage Rijndijk at Spanjaardsbrug to cars and buses 17 August–11 September 2026, detours traffic, preserves emergency/cycle/moped passage and gives direction-specific Baanderij access. It overlaps the 3 September audit time and T+72 but has no matching public-context record. Two A4 links are one physical corridor; N445/N446 are fragments. The graph omits bridge operations/local approaches, and 44 GTFS stops plus zero NDW matches do not prove operation or openness.
findings.action: Ingest authoritative planned/current restrictions with issue/start/end time, geometry, direction, mode, emergency exemption, detour, lifecycle and licence. Apply only against an explicit exercise clock; calendar-unbound presets remain labelled synthetic. Build a non-additive physical-corridor/local-bridge graph with unit-bearing capacity, passability and emergency priority.

findings.summary: Alrijne's regional acute-care role and other non-resident activity are neither demand nor verified continuity.

These establish a critical destination and regional inbound dependency, not live patients, staff, occupancy, acceptance, ambulance access, backup, fuel or supply. findings.action: Keep official residents authoritative and separate clearly labelled, timestamped non-resident activity/demand under CORR-015. Bind privacy-safe live/official-range hospital acceptance, staffing, backup endurance and ambulance/supply access only through authorized interfaces; otherwise retain Unknown and scenario assumptions.

findings.summary: Exact eight-service availability lacks verified utility, telecom, water/drainage, facility and supply topology or state.
findings.evidence: Compound T+24 emits eight exact values from 0.151092 to 0.820000. One Liander planning sample, twelve incomplete water objects, 42 antenna sites, seventeen schools, 44 transit stops, four boundary links and one annual hospital record do not provide feeder/customer or pipe topology, compatible capacity, live load/pressure/backhaul, damage, priority users, backup, switching, repair crews or restoration commitments. Absent source is Unknown/no selected event, not observed smoke or proof of no local ignition.

findings.summary: River/compound plateaus and exact recovery across other presets lack first-72-hour actions and resources.
findings.evidence: River stress/severity and seven services freeze T+24–72 while affected rises and Facilities worsens. Compound severity/cyber decline while pressure, stress, 17,709 affected and every service remain exactly fixed. Coastal direct water clears while 4,021 remain affected; storm/pluvial/winter/wildfire direct effects clear with exact residual services. findings.action: Require a typed incident/action/resource ledger at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 with authority/owner, target, prerequisite, route, crew/material/fuel/water, start/end, state, observation/valid time and uncertainty. findings.summary: Official stress scenarios, dated restrictions, schedules, missing screens and synthetic outputs need adjacent provenance and NoData gates.
findings.evidence: The UI can juxtapose annual CBS, 2023–2028 plans/stress scenarios, incomplete assets, a current road closure, bridge schedules, one grid-planning sample, registers, no local water/weather/road/air/seismic observations and exact synthetic values. Use an explicit reference clock; stale/future state deactivates, missing matches render Unknown, and normalized inundation stress is never labelled depth/metres.

residualLimitations: Complete electricity, gas, drinking-water, sewer/drainage, telecom, care and supply topology, control logic, live load/outage, backup, crews, spares, fuel and restoration state are unavailable or security-sensitive; public geometry, plans and territories cannot replace them.

No selected Rijnland/WMCN/LIWO case establishes a GM0547 primary or regional defence breach, boezem/polder boundary, terrain-connected footprint, depth/velocity, arrival or recession. A generic value is not evidence and no selected case is not safe.

Municipal climate stress-test products and IWKp are valuable official scenario/programme evidence but require native machine files, edition, event/antecedent state, CRS, units, licence, lifecycle and explicit NoData before analytical use.

The HWH screen contains twelve heterogeneous objects with missing or non-comparable capacities and no complete catchment/sewer/defence topology, settings, maintenance, power/backup, current state or event capacity.
No local Waterinfo observation/forecast point is assigned. Missing point/horizon coverage cannot be spatialized, held constant or treated as zero through T+72.

Four NWB boundary links, local bridge/approach omissions, 44 GTFS stops and zero NDW situations do not establish scenario-time operation, passability, emergency priority, detours, destination or throughput. Repeated A4 sections are not independent redundancy.
